title_a: Mem0: Building production-ready AI agents with scalable long-term memory
title_b: Zep: A temporal knowledge graph architecture for agent memory
claim_a: Graph memory adds minimal value over vector memory on the LoCoMo benchmark
claim_b: Temporal knowledge graph achieves 18.5% improvement over vector approaches on LongMemEval
annotation_notes: Both papers evaluate graph vs vector memory approaches. Mem0 reports minimal gains from graph memory; Zep demonstrates substantial improvements. Core research question is identical; conclusions are opposite.

title_a: Mem0: Building production-ready AI agents with scalable long-term memory
title_b: Optimizing the Interface Between Knowledge Graphs and LLMs for Complex Reasoning
claim_a: Selective memory with vector retrieval is sufficient for production AI agents
claim_b: Graph-RAG achieves 92.5% accuracy on multi-hop queries versus 60% for flat RAG
annotation_notes: Mem0 advocates vector-only approaches for production. Cognee demonstrates a 32.5pp gap favouring graph memory on multi-hop tasks. Indirect because Mem0 does not specifically test multi-hop reasoning.

title_a: Zep: A temporal knowledge graph architecture for agent memory
title_b: Optimizing the Interface Between Knowledge Graphs and LLMs for Complex Reasoning
claim_a: Temporal knowledge graph achieves substantial improvements over vector-only approaches
claim_b: Hybrid graph-vector memory significantly outperforms flat RAG on complex reasoning
annotation_notes: Both papers agree graph-based memory outperforms vector-only approaches. They use different benchmarks and architectures but converge on the same conclusion.

title_a: Graph-Native Cognitive Memory for AI Agents: Formal Belief Revision Semantics
title_b: Zep: A temporal knowledge graph architecture for agent memory
claim_a: Existing graph memory systems lack formal belief revision correspondence and URI addressing
claim_b: Temporal knowledge graph with bitemporal versioning improves agent memory recall
annotation_notes: Kumiho extends Graphiti by adding formal belief revision semantics. Kumiho explicitly acknowledges Graphiti as prior work and builds upon it. Not a contradiction.

title_a: Belief Revision: The Adaptability of Large Language Models Reasoning
title_b: Graph-Native Cognitive Memory for AI Agents: Formal Belief Revision Semantics
claim_a: LLMs handle belief revision through prompt-level mechanisms when confronted with new evidence
claim_b: Belief revision in AI agents requires graph-native mutable state, not prompt-level artifacts
annotation_notes: The 2024 paper studies LLM belief revision through prompting. The 2026 paper argues this is insufficient and proposes graph-native belief revision. Extension not contradiction — different architectural level.

title_a: Think Locally, Explain Globally: Graph-Guided LLM Investigations
title_b: Belief Revision: The Adaptability of Large Language Models Reasoning
claim_a: Existing belief-centric systems treat beliefs as prompt-level artifacts and lack explicit mechanisms for revision under contradictory evidence
claim_b: LLMs can adaptively revise prior beliefs through prompting when new evidence is presented
annotation_notes: The 2026 paper explicitly critiques prompt-level belief revision as insufficient. The 2024 paper evaluates exactly this capability and presents it as a valid approach. Indirect contradiction on methodology.

title_a: From Local to Global: A Graph RAG Approach to Query-Focused Summarization
title_b: Optimizing the Interface Between Knowledge Graphs and LLMs for Complex Reasoning
claim_a: Graph-based RAG substantially outperforms naive RAG on global queries requiring synthesis across many documents
claim_b: Graph-RAG achieves 92.5% accuracy on multi-hop queries versus 60% for flat RAG baselines
annotation_notes: Both papers agree graph-based RAG outperforms flat RAG. GraphRAG focuses on summarisation tasks; Cognee on multi-hop reasoning. Consistent direction of effect.

title_a: A Survey on Temporal Knowledge Graph Completion: Taxonomy, Progress, and Prospects
title_b: Zep: A temporal knowledge graph architecture for agent memory
claim_a: Temporal knowledge graph completion requires modelling time-varying facts with temporal embeddings
claim_b: Bitemporal versioning with valid_at and invalid_at timestamps enables accurate temporal agent memory
annotation_notes: The survey describes temporal KG completion methods. Zep applies temporal KG concepts to agent memory. Extension of the field to a new application domain.

title_a: TempoQR: Temporal Question Reasoning over Knowledge Graphs
title_b: GraphWalker: Agentic Knowledge Graph Question Answering via Synthetic Trajectory Curriculum
claim_a: Temporal questions over knowledge graphs require specialised reasoning about time intervals
claim_b: Agentic graph traversal with synthetic trajectory curriculum outperforms static KG-QA methods
annotation_notes: TempoQR establishes temporal KG-QA as a problem. GraphWalker proposes a newer agentic approach. Extension not contradiction — GraphWalker does not specifically address the temporal dimension TempoQR focuses on.

title_a: Mem0: Building production-ready AI agents with scalable long-term memory
title_b: Graph-Native Cognitive Memory for AI Agents: Formal Belief Revision Semantics
claim_a: Selective vector memory is sufficient for production AI agent long-term memory needs
claim_b: Production agent memory requires graph-native mutable state with formal belief revision for correctness
annotation_notes: Mem0 advocates vector-only selective memory as sufficient for production. The 2026 paper argues this architecture is fundamentally insufficient for belief revision. Temporal obsolescence — Mem0's claim may have been reasonable at publication time but is challenged by the later paper.
